For personal

What it’s like to have your own agent.

One agent, on your own computer, quietly working through the inbox, the calendar, the errands, and the research you never get to.

Quietly sorting the inbox checking the calendar drafting a reply gathering research sorting the inbox

Archie is in testing, Mac and Windows both, and not for sale yet. The waitlist hears the moment that changes.

Join the waitlist

Which one is this?

One person · you are here

Free on your own AI account for one agent, no card. Up to 10 agents for $30 a month or $299 a year, and each one answers you.

A team

Up to 50 agents, and any of them can answer your whole team. That is Archie for Business: $99 a month, or $999 a year. Same app to learn, same computer it runs on.

The idea

Your own agent, on your own computer.

Archie is a desktop app that runs your own AI agent. You talk to it the way you’d text a friend.

Your files, agent settings and keys stay on your computer. On your own AI key, conversations go directly to your AI provider from each agent’s next start. The app needs an active license; canceling a plan does not delete your data.

What your agent takes on

The small stuff, handled.

The repetitive work, off your plate: it drafts, sorts, and reminds. Email goes out only when you send it or set a time.

Email & InboxFlags priority messages and proposes ready-to-send replies
Scheduling & RemindersSuggests best slots and drafts confirmation messages
Research & LookupsBuilds ranked lists and summarizes options with next steps
Lists & TrackingKeeps running lists (follow-ups, applications, plans) and answers questions about them
Following Up with ContactsPrepares personalized check-ins using recent context
Daily BriefingsSurfaces your schedule, priority emails, and key reminders each morning

Nearest to your week

You bill by the hour, so the hour you lose chasing people is the one that costs twice.

  • SkillWaiting On Every reply that never came, and every invoice nobody paid.
  • SkillCommitment Keeper Reads your sent mail for every “I’ll send that over”.
  • SkillFind a Time Reads your calendar and drafts the reply that ends the back and forth.

Four schedules, one of them yours, and the school mail nobody has opened.

  • SkillSchool & Family Pulls the dates and the what-to-bring out of the school mail.
  • SkillCalendar Manager Proposes the move, and makes it once you approve.
  • SkillBirthday & Anniversary Keeper Every date that matters, early enough to do something.

Everything still has to happen, and you are doing it on four hours of sleep.

  • PersonalityNew Parent Written for one hand, at three in the morning.
  • SkillMedication & Refill Reminder What to take, the dose, and when the refill runs out.
  • SkillMeal Planner The week’s meals out of whatever is in the fridge.

You leave the appointment and half of what was said has already gone.

  • SkillHealth Record Tell it what the doctor said and it keeps the thread.
  • SkillMedication & Refill Reminder The list, the doses, and the refill dates.
  • SkillPaperwork Benefits and enrollments, step by step, with the next one named.

None of it is hard. It is that no one thing reminds you of any of it.

  • SkillHome Maintenance The jobs nobody remembers: furnace filters, drains, the gutters.
  • SkillWarranty & Returns When you bought it, and the day the return window shuts.
  • RoutineWeekly Home Check Says a job is due two weeks out, safety first, and stays quiet otherwise.

You know roughly what comes in. What goes out is spread over eleven websites.

  • SkillBills & Subscriptions Everything that charges you on a repeat, with real dates.
  • SkillMoney In & Out Log what you spent as you go, then ask how much is left.
  • RoutineBill Reminders Three days out, before the late fee rather than after it.

Three out of 160, all included. Whichever you pick, the limits are the same: no email goes out until you approve it, a calendar change is proposed and applied only after you approve it, and none of them can spend money. The whole list, and how to check it →

Building your agent

Shape your agent piece by piece.

Archie is modular. Your agent arrives working, asks what your days look like, and fits its own pieces from your answers. Every one of them is yours to swap, remove, or add to.

Personality

How your agent talks to you. Warm and chatty or brief and to the point.

Skills

The things it can do. Add one in a click from the marketplace, or say what you wish it could do and Archie writes the skill.

Routines

Things it does on its own, on a schedule. A briefing every morning, a report every Friday, without being asked.

Knowledge Base

Give it your files (notes, PDFs, documents) so it answers from what you know, not just what it was trained on. The same tab holds its memory: what it has picked up about you, every line yours to read, add to or delete.

Connections

Link the tools you already use, like Gmail, Outlook, iCloud and your calendar, only ever when you say so.

All of it saves to one file, under Moving and backups: your skills, what your agent remembers, your routines. Put it on another computer and it picks up where this one left off. No key is in it, so you get a list of what to connect again. It is an ordinary file, not a sealed one, so keep it where you would keep a tax return. What travels and what does not →

Say hello

This is Ember.

Ember is the face your agents wear. Every agent you make gets its own: a color, a hat, a pair of eyes, dealt from the agent itself, so two agents on one computer never look like twins. Change any of it, or hand over a photo of your own instead.

What the plan runs

Ten agents, every add-on, one person.

The whole catalog is included. What decides whether this edition fits you is the last word in that heading.

Up to 10 agents

Run one that watches the inbox and another that keeps the follow-up list, or one for work and one for the house. Every one of the 160 add-ons is included, not sold separately, and new ones arrive for everyone.

One person per agent

A personal Archie agent answers one person: its owner. That is enforced in the app, not a policy, so there is no second seat to buy on this plan. If somebody else needs to message the same agent, that is Archie for Business, which lifts the ceiling on each of them.

Your computer, your AI account

Your conversations, your files and your calendar live on your own computer and go straight to your AI provider on your own account. They never pass through an Otian server. Everything we can and can’t see, line by line.

Getting started

On your own, or with us beside you.

Either way it ends up on your computer, under your accounts, with you able to change it.

On your own

Install Archie, sign in, and it walks you through the first agent. How It Works has the five steps and what you need before you start. Nothing to pay us beyond the plan.

With us beside you

An hour together, connecting an inbox, a calendar and a chat app. You leave able to run and change it yourself. That is guided setup, $250 an hour, and it starts with a free call.
